introduction: ERC-1328 defines a URI format for encoding the data needed to open a connection between an application and a wallet. It was proposed by ligi and Pedro Gomes in August 2018. A request uses the wc scheme followed by a topic string, an @-delimited version number, and a query string of parameters: v1 URIs carry a bridge URL and a symmetric key, while v2 URIs carry a symKey and a relay-protocol. Because the payload is a compact URI rather than JSON, it can be shown as a QR code or link and parsed efficiently by wallets.
designPurpose: ERC-1328 was designed to replace the JSON payload used by the alpha version of the WalletConnect protocol, which parsed inefficiently from a QR code. By encoding the connection data as a URI instead, the standard gives wallets a compact, unambiguous string that QR-code scanners and deep-link handlers can read directly, and it lets the Android intent system route the link to a wallet. A required version segment lets the parameter set change across protocol versions while preserving backwards compatibility.
commonUsage: The format is used by the WalletConnect protocol to pair mobile wallets with applications: a dApp renders the URI as a QR code, and a wallet scans or opens it to derive the shared session parameters. Version 1 URIs supply a bridge URL and encryption key, while version 2 URIs supply a relay protocol and a symmetric key for the pairing topic, plus an optional expiry timestamp. Wallet SDKs, dApp connector libraries, and QR-code components across the ecosystem parse this URI to bootstrap an encrypted session.
sim.connectionUriWalkthrough.name: Connection URI Walkthrough
sim.connectionUriWalkthrough.desc: Follow a WalletConnect URI from a dApp through a QR scan to an established pairing session.
sim.connectionUriWalkthrough.step.build: The application creates a connection request and selects the WalletConnect protocol version to use.
sim.connectionUriWalkthrough.step.encode: The topic, version, and parameters are encoded into a wc: URI that can be shown as a QR code or a link.
sim.connectionUriWalkthrough.step.scan: The wallet user scans or opens the URI, and the wallet parses the topic, version, and connection parameters before approving the pairing.
sim.connectionUriWalkthrough.step.pair: The wallet derives the shared encryption key and relay settings from the URI, establishing the pairing session with the application.
